nodes.label: Claim-level Verification
nodes.rationale: Individual claims are the basic unit; evidence cards link back to source locations.

nodes.label: Direct Evidence Requirement
nodes.rationale: Positive or negative conclusions are withheld when direct source evidence cannot be verified.

nodes.label: Evidence Traceability Principle
nodes.rationale: The product helps users trace and compare claims and evidence instead of declaring unsupported absolute truth.

nodes.label: Avoid Unneeded 3D Effects
nodes.rationale: Effects must not distract from evidence reading; unused 3D packages should not be forced into the screen.

nodes.label: Evidence Research Workspace
nodes.rationale: The product should be a calm research workspace for reading and comparing evidence rather than a generic dashboard.

nodes.label: Explicit Demo Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Synthetic examples and demo states should not be mistaken for live verification.

nodes.label: Mobile Selection Persistence
nodes.rationale: Switching mobile views should preserve the selected item.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion
nodes.rationale: Selection and entrance transitions should respect reduced-motion settings.

nodes.label: Grounded Answer Synthesis
nodes.rationale: A fifth LLM stage summarizes verified source text while preserving existing claim verdicts and grounding citations in source bodies.

nodes.label: YouTube Data Exclusion
nodes.rationale: YouTube titles and public comments are excluded from synthesis evidence even when shown as context.

nodes.label: Citation Source Grounding
nodes.rationale: Every substantive answer block requires a citation whose exact quote appears in an eligible verified source body.

nodes.label: Grounded Answer Synthesis
nodes.rationale: A separate post-verification synthesis call provides a source-grounded overview without changing fact verdicts.

nodes.label: User Consent Scope
nodes.rationale: Synthesis uses existing consent and server-side provider keys without adding a key or persistence store.

nodes.label: YouTube Exclusion Policy
nodes.rationale: YouTube captions, video content, replies, and public comments are not synthesis evidence or model input.

nodes.label: User Consent Gate
nodes.rationale: Only consented verification requests are sent to external services.

nodes.label: YouTube Evidence Exclusion Policy
nodes.rationale: Video titles and public comments are display context only; comments are excluded from claim-verification input, evidence, and JSON export.

nodes.label: Local Development Boundary
nodes.rationale: The unauthenticated API is for local/personal verification and must not be exposed publicly.

nodes.label: No Persistent Answer Storage
nodes.rationale: The design does not introduce persistent storage for source text or synthesis answers.

nodes.label: Server Credential Boundary
nodes.rationale: Provider credentials remain server-side and are not exposed through browser/public variables.

nodes.label: Untrusted Source Data Boundary
nodes.rationale: User text and web pages are untrusted data; embedded instructions are not system or tool instructions.

nodes.label: User Consent Gate
nodes.rationale: Original text and focus are sent to providers and web search only within user consent.

nodes.label: Data Mode
nodes.rationale: Data Mode uses data-router APIs without the Framework Vite plugin or route-module convention.

nodes.label: Declarative Data API Boundary
nodes.rationale: Data loading, actions, fetchers, and pending UI require a Data or Framework mode rather than a Declarative router.

nodes.label: Declarative Mode
nodes.rationale: Declarative Mode uses router components and JSX routes and lacks data-router features.

nodes.label: Framework Mode
nodes.rationale: Framework Mode is the full-stack mode built around the React Router Vite plugin, route config, modules, generated types, and rendering strategies.

nodes.label: Server-only Module Boundary
nodes.rationale: Server-only/database code should remain outside browser-rendered component code.

nodes.label: RSC Data Mode

nodes.label: RSC Framework Mode
nodes.rationale: Framework RSC uses a distinct unstable Vite plugin and server-component route exports.

nodes.label: RSC Stability Policy
nodes.rationale: RSC APIs are unstable; check installed versions and existing entry/config patterns before changes.

nodes.label: Data Mode

nodes.label: Declarative Mode
nodes.rationale: Declarative Mode uses router components and JSX routes without data-router loaders, actions, or fetchers.

nodes.label: Framework Mode
nodes.rationale: Framework Mode combines the Vite plugin, route modules, generated types, and full-stack rendering options.

nodes.label: Mode-aware Guidance
nodes.rationale: Router APIs and conventions differ by mode, so identify the application mode and use matching guidance.

nodes.rationale: A future forecast is not resolved as a present fact; whether it was stated can be checked separately.

nodes.label: Seven Verdict Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: The proposal separates supported, partial, missing-context, conflicting, insufficient, not-checkable, and contradicted outcomes.

nodes.label: Forecast Uncertainty Policy
nodes.rationale: Forecast answers must not invent probabilities, consensus, or opposing views absent source support.
